newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica signs deal for refinery sale.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica signs deal for refinery sale.

text.p: Jamaica's government on Wednesday signed an agreement to divest state-owned Petrojam to a group led by its management and staff, a government spokesman said Thursday.

Prime Minister P.J. Patterson had announced in July that Jamaica had accepted the bid from employees, Austin Blades Finance Ltd. and Americar Trading Corp. to buy the refinery and its subsidiaries for US$68 million.

With the signing of the deal yesterday, US$59 million became payable within 30 days. In addition to the refinery, which has a production capacity of 36,000 barrels per day, the sale included the Petcom chain of local gas stations, several cargo vessels, an ethanol plant and a sugar factory in Belize.
The government will maintain a minority shareholding, and employees will be offered no less than 22 percent of the total equity within the next six months.
